scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Shagging on the Boulevard: The Carolina Beach Dance
This is Carolina shag. 1940s.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Carolina shag · United States · 1940s

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The term 'Carolina shag' is associated with Cherry Grove Beach, South Carolina, and Carolina Beach, North Carolina, emerging during the 1940s.
According to historian Bo Bryan, the shag descended from the Carolina Jitterbug and the Little Apple, which evolved from the 1937 Big Apple in Columbia, South Carolina.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance serves as a major regional cultural symbol, becoming South Carolina's official state dance in 1984 and North Carolina's official popular dance in 2005.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Learn To Dance The Carolina Shag (https://archive.org/details/learn-to-dance-the-carolina-shag)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a slot using a six-count, eight-step basic pattern.
Dancers execute two triple steps followed by a rock step, counted as 'one-and-two, three-and-four, five-six'.
The first two triple-step sections take roughly the same amount of time as the final rock-step count.
Watch for Basic Step.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Slotted path between partners

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Carolina shag is danced to beach music, primarily vintage R&B in 4/4 time signature ranging from 100 to over 130 beats per minute.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 115 beats a minute.
Mid-tempo vintage R&B and beach music playing in 4/4 time between 100 and 130+ BPM.
